_doc: Curated parity notes per service. status: full | partial | stub | paid | unsupported | data-plane. Edit by hand; build_catalog.py does not regenerate this file.

account.notes: 4 operations: GetAccountInformation, GetContactInformation, ListRegions, GetRegionOptStatus. Returns AccountState=ACTIVE; 31-region opt-in matrix with 14 opt-in-required regions.
gotchas: No AccountScopedDict — state is global, not per-account
No persistence — state is not saved across restarts
ContactInformation is hardcoded, not configurable
Regions list is static — opt-in/opt-out actions are not supported

acm.notes: 12 operations: RequestCertificate, DescribeCertificate, ListCertificates, DeleteCertificate, GetCertificate, ImportCertificate, AddTagsToCertificate, RemoveTagsFromCertificate, ListTagsForCertificate, UpdateCertificateOptions, RenewCertificate, ResendValidationEmail.
gotchas: RequestCertificate issues immediately in ISSUED state — no DNS/email validation wait
Certificates are synthetic PEM placeholders, not real X.509 — ASN.1 parsing will fail
PrivateKey is stripped from persisted state — re-import required after restart for IMPORTED certs
ImportCertificate does not parse CN/SAN from the cert body — DomainName is synthetic
RenewCertificate and ResendValidationEmail are no-ops

alb.notes: 30 actions covering load balancers, target groups, listeners, rules, target registration, and tags. Data-plane rule matching with path-pattern, host-header, http-method, query-string conditions. Lambda target invocation for target type 'lambda'. Fixed-response and redirect actions supported. SetSubnets / SetIpAddressType / SetSecurityGroups now implemented per botocore output shapes (SetSubnets → AvailabilityZones + IpAddressType, SetIpAddressType → IpAddressType, SetSecurityGroups → SecurityGroupIds — note: not SecurityGroups).
gotchas: Only lambda target type is supported for forwarding — instance and ip targets are registered but not routable
source-ip condition always matches — no real network layer
Health checks always report targets as healthy
No real load balancing — first matching listener is used

apigateway.notes: Module aggregator — see apigateway_v1 / apigateway_v2. HTTP API and WebSocket API; Lambda proxy / HTTP proxy / MOCK; data plane via {apiId}.execute-api.localhost or path-based /_aws/execute-api/{apiId}/{stage}/{path}; $default stage served from URL root; per-API CORS; request parameter mapping; JWT data-plane authorization with RS256 signature verification; qualified-alias integration URIs; WebSocket data plane with @connections management API (PostToConnection/GetConnection/DeleteConnection); route responses and integration responses; pin apiId via ms-custom-id tag. JWT authorizer resolves the issuer's `jwks_uri` via OIDC discovery (`{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration`) so non-Cognito issuers (Salesforce `/id/keys`, Okta `/oauth2/v1/keys`, etc.) work; Cognito short-circuits to the local pool JWKS; conventional `/.well-known/jwks.json` is the fallback when discovery is unavailable. Discovery results cached per-issuer for 2h.
gotchas: JWT authorizer only supports RS256 algorithm — other algorithms are not verified
JWKS cache is per-account — issuer URL collisions across accounts may serve different keys
WebSocket connections are in-process only and not persisted across restarts
HTTP_PROXY timeout defaults to 30s (configurable via MINISTACK_APIGW_PROXY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)

apigateway_v1.notes: REST API protocol with 60+ control-plane operations. Resources, methods, integrations, method/integration responses, deployments, stages, authorizers, models, API keys, usage plans, usage plan keys, domain names, base path mappings, tags, and account settings. Data plane with resource tree matching ({param} and {proxy+}), Lambda proxy format 1.0, HTTP proxy, MOCK integrations. JSON Patch for all PATCH operations. UpdateStage supports method-level settings (metrics, logging, throttling, caching). Pin id via ms-custom-id tag.
gotchas: API key validation is not enforced on the data plane — apiKeyRequired is stored but not checked
Authorizer Lambda invocation is not implemented on the v1 data plane
Usage plan quotas and throttling are not enforced
Pagination uses opaque base64url tokens with a max of 500 items per page

appconfig.notes: 33 operations covering control plane + data plane. Applications, environments, configuration profiles, hosted configuration versions, deployment strategies, deployments, tags. Data plane: StartConfigurationSession + GetLatestConfiguration with token rotation. Deployments complete immediately.
gotchas: Deployments complete immediately — no gradual rollout, no bake time enforcement
Configuration session tokens are single-use — each GetLatestConfiguration consumes and rotates the token
Accepts botocore's misspelled /deployementstrategies path alongside the correct /deploymentstrategies

appsync.notes: GraphQL API management: CreateGraphQLApi, GetGraphQLApi, ListGraphQLApis, UpdateGraphQLApi, DeleteGraphQLApi; API keys, data sources (DynamoDB, Lambda, HTTP, Elasticsearch, RelationalDB), resolvers (UNIT and PIPELINE), types, tags. GraphQL data plane auto-resolves DynamoDB and Lambda data sources — get/list/create/update/delete operations inferred from field name prefixes. AWS_LAMBDA data sources receive the full AWS-standard AppSyncResolverEvent (arguments, source, request.headers, prev, stash, info.{fieldName,parentTypeName,variables}); AWS_LAMBDA auth mode invokes the authorizer Lambda first and threads its resolverContext into event.identity. Authorizer event matches the verbatim AWS shape (authorizationToken + requestHeaders + requestContext with apiId/accountId/requestId/queryString/operationName/variables). Authorizer returning isAuthorized:false, an unreachable authorizer, or one that raises all surface as UnauthorizedException (HTTP 401). Unhandled resolver exceptions surface as GraphQL errors entries instead of leaking RIE error payloads as data.
gotchas: GraphQL data plane uses heuristic field-name matching (get*, list*, create*, update*, delete*) — custom resolver mapping templates are not executed
VTL request/response mapping templates are stored but not evaluated
No schema validation — any SDL string is accepted without parsing

appsync_events.notes: AppSync Event APIs under /v2/apis. Control plane: CRUD for APIs, channel namespaces, API keys. Data plane: HTTP publish on POST /event and WebSocket realtime on {apiId}.appsync-realtime-api.* using aws-appsync-event-ws subprotocol. Connection-scoped authorization via header-<base64> entry. AWS_LAMBDA authorizer invocation supported. Channel path validation (1..5 segments). Set APPSYNC_EVENTS_ENFORCE_AUTH=1 for strict mode.
gotchas: Realtime connections are in-process only — not persisted across restarts
Max 5 events per publish batch (matches AWS spec)
Subscribe wildcard only supports single-level trailing * — no multi-level globbing
Keep-alive interval defaults to 60s (configurable via APPSYNC_EVENTS_KA_INTERVAL_SECS)

athena.notes: 30 operations: query execution (Start/Get/Stop/List/BatchGet), workgroups (Create/Delete/Get/List/Update), named queries (Create/Delete/Get/List/BatchGet), data catalogs (Create/Get/List/Delete/Update), prepared statements (Create/Get/Delete/List), table metadata (Get/List stubs), tags (Tag/Untag/List). Real SQL via DuckDB when installed (pip install duckdb) with Glue catalog integration and S3 path rewriting; otherwise mock results. Result pagination with column type metadata. Query results written to S3 as CSV.
gotchas: DuckDB queries run in-memory per query — no shared catalog state between queries
Table metadata endpoints (GetTableMetadata, ListTableMetadata) return stubs, not real schema
S3 path rewriting maps s3:// URIs to local filesystem paths
Without DuckDB installed, all queries return mock/hardcoded results

autoscaling.notes: 23 actions; in-memory state, no real instance scaling. Full ASG lifecycle: launch configs, scaling policies, lifecycle hooks (Put/Describe/Delete/Complete/RecordHeartbeat), scheduled actions, tags (CreateOrUpdate/Describe/Delete). CDK/Terraform compatible.
gotchas: No actual instances are launched or terminated — DesiredCapacity is stored but not acted on
DescribeAutoScalingInstances always returns empty — no synthetic instance records
DescribeScalingActivities always returns empty — no scaling activity tracking
Lifecycle hook actions (Complete/RecordHeartbeat) are no-ops

backup.notes: 19 operations: vaults (Create/Describe/Delete/List), plans (Create/Get/Update/Delete/List/ListVersions), selections (Create/Get/Delete/List), jobs (Start/Stop/Describe/List), tags (Tag/Untag/List). In-memory; jobs complete immediately with COMPLETED state. Vaults and plans participate in Resource Groups Tagging API.
gotchas: Backup jobs complete instantly — no actual data backup occurs
Recovery points are synthetic ARNs with no real data behind them
StartBackupJob ignores the resource — no validation that the resource exists

batch.notes: 9 operations: compute environments (Create/Describe), job queues (Create/Describe), job definitions (Register/Describe with multi-revision), jobs (Submit/Describe/List). Control-plane stub — submitted jobs immediately transition to SUCCEEDED. Job queue lookup by name or ARN.
gotchas: All submitted jobs immediately SUCCEED — no actual container execution
No job state transitions (SUBMITTED -> PENDING -> RUNNABLE -> etc.)
No delete operations for compute environments or job queues

cloudformation.notes: Stack lifecycle, 15 intrinsics, 83 resource types; some resources couple directly to service modules. AppConfig CFN surface complete: Application + Environment + ConfigurationProfile + HostedConfigurationVersion + DeploymentStrategy + Deployment, with Ref / Fn::GetAtt return values (EnvironmentId; ConfigurationProfileId + KmsKeyArn; VersionNumber; Id; DeploymentNumber + State) matching the AWS reference. HostedConfigurationVersion enforces the optional LatestVersionNumber locking token; Deployment tags stored against the AWS-shape ARN.

cloudfront.notes: Distributions (Create/CreateWithTags/Get/GetConfig/List/Update/Delete), invalidations (Create/List/Get), OAC (Create/Get/GetConfig/List/Update/Delete), CloudFront Functions (Create/Delete/Describe/Get/List/Publish/Update), KeyValueStore (Create/Describe/List/Update/Delete), tags (Tag/Untag/List). ETag-based optimistic concurrency on all mutating operations. CallerReference idempotency on CreateDistribution. Also SaaS Manager multi-tenant distributions (connection groups + distribution tenants).
gotchas: Distributions deploy instantly — no real CDN edge propagation
CloudFront Functions code is stored but not executed
Invalidations complete immediately
No actual HTTP caching or origin fetching — distribution is metadata-only

cloudfront_keyvaluestore.notes: Separate cloudfront-keyvaluestore SDK service. 6 operations: DescribeKeyValueStore, ListKeys, GetKey, PutKey, DeleteKey, UpdateKeys. ETag-based optimistic concurrency on every mutating op; UpdateKeys is atomic (validate-then-commit). ListKeys paginates with opaque NextToken capped at 50.
gotchas: KVS data is lazily initialized from the CloudFront _kvstores control-plane record
ImportSource on create is accepted but no actual S3 data import is performed

cloudtrail.notes: 12 operations: LookupEvents (audit log), CreateTrail, DeleteTrail, GetTrail, DescribeTrails, GetTrailStatus, StartLogging, StopLogging, PutEventSelectors, GetEventSelectors, AddTags, ListTags, RemoveTags. Recording off by default — enable with CLOUDTRAIL_RECORDING=1. Per-account ring buffer capped at CLOUDTRAIL_MAX_EVENTS (default 10000).
gotchas: Event recording is off by default — must set CLOUDTRAIL_RECORDING=1
Events are stored in a per-account ring buffer, not delivered to S3
GetTrailStatus returns synthetic data, not real delivery metrics
Metric data is stored but no actual alarm evaluation or metric math is performed

cloudwatch_logs.notes: FilterLogEvents supports * / ? globs, multi-term AND, -term exclusion.
gotchas: No real-time subscription filters — logs are stored but not streamed to destinations
Log retention is stored but not enforced — old log events are never automatically deleted

codebuild.notes: 11 operations: CreateProject, BatchGetProjects, ListProjects, UpdateProject, DeleteProject, StartBuild, BatchGetBuilds, StopBuild, ListBuilds, ListBuildsForProject, BatchDeleteBuilds.
gotchas: Builds complete immediately — no actual code compilation or container execution
Build logs are not generated

cognito.notes: 50+ operations covering both cognito-idp (User Pools) and cognito-identity (Identity Pools). User pool lifecycle, clients, users (admin and self-service), groups, auth flows (AdminInitiateAuth, InitiateAuth, SignUp, ConfirmSignUp, ForgotPassword), domains, identity providers (OIDC/SAML), MFA (TOTP), tags. CUSTOM_AUTH flow wired through DefineAuthChallenge / CreateAuthChallenge / VerifyAuthChallengeResponse Lambda triggers for passwordless / magic-link / SMS-OTP; session token opaque to client, TTL honors AuthSessionValidity (minutes), capped at 3 answered rounds per AWS. The IDP / Identity dispatchers are async and run sync handlers via asyncio.to_thread, so trigger Lambdas (which call back into ministack over HTTP) don't deadlock against a blocked event loop. Issues real JWTs signed with RSA keys; JWKS endpoint at /{poolId}/.well-known/jwks.json.
gotchas: JWTs are locally signed — not interchangeable with real AWS Cognito tokens
Email/SMS verification is auto-confirmed — no actual delivery
Identity pool credentials are synthetic — no real STS federation

cur.notes: 7 operations: PutReportDefinition, DeleteReportDefinition, DescribeReportDefinitions, ModifyReportDefinition, ListTagsForResource, TagResource, UntagResource. Cost & Usage Report definitions stored in-memory; no real billing data generated.
gotchas: No actual cost or usage data is generated — report definitions are metadata-only

dynamodb.notes: 26+ operations: CreateTable, DeleteTable, DescribeTable, ListTables, UpdateTable, PutItem, GetItem, DeleteItem, UpdateItem, Query, Scan, BatchWriteItem, BatchGetItem, TransactWriteItems, TransactGetItems, DescribeTimeToLive, UpdateTimeToLive, DescribeContinuousBackups, UpdateContinuousBackups, DescribeEndpoints, TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsOfResource, EnableKinesisStreamingDestination, DisableKinesisStreamingDestination, DescribeKinesisStreamingDestination, UpdateKinesisStreamingDestination, ExportTableToPointInTime, DescribeExport, ListExports, ImportTable, DescribeImport, ListImports, ExecuteStatement (PartiQL). TTL enforced via thread-safe background reaper (60s cadence). DynamoDB Streams emit INSERT/MODIFY/REMOVE records on all write operations, respects StreamViewType. Kinesis streaming destinations fan item mutations into any Kinesis stream by ARN. ExportTableToPointInTime / ImportTable return IN_PROGRESS at submit time and flip to COMPLETED only after MINISTACK_DDB_EXPORT_COMPLETE_AFTER_SEC / MINISTACK_DDB_IMPORT_COMPLETE_AFTER_SEC (default 1s) has elapsed — matching real AWS, which always reports IN_PROGRESS at submit. PartiQL UPDATE/DELETE require an = clause on every primary-key attribute (else ValidationException); non-key WHERE clauses act as a conditional check on the targeted item (missing item or failing non-key predicate → ConditionalCheckFailedException, item unchanged) instead of silently no-op'ing. Legacy conditional parameters (Expected, KeyConditions, ScanFilter, QueryFilter) supported.
gotchas: TTL enforcement runs on 60s cadence, not real-time — items may persist up to 60s past expiry
PartiQL support covers SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE but not all expression features
No provisioned throughput enforcement — reads/writes are unlimited
Single synthetic shard per DynamoDB Stream — no shard splitting
Export/Import grace window is fixed at submit time — for fast tests, set MINISTACK_DDB_EXPORT_COMPLETE_AFTER_SEC / MINISTACK_DDB_IMPORT_COMPLETE_AFTER_SEC to a small value (e.g. 0.05)

dynamodb_streams.notes: 4 operations: ListStreams, DescribeStream, GetShardIterator, GetRecords. Stream records emitted by dynamodb writes; shares dynamodb credential scope. Single synthetic shard per stream.
gotchas: No AccountScopedDict — reads directly from the dynamodb module's stream state
Single synthetic shard per stream — no shard splitting modeled
Not in _state_map — no independent persistence (streams live inside dynamodb state)

ec2.notes: 80+ actions covering instances, images (stub), security groups, key pairs, VPCs, subnets, availability zones, internet gateways, elastic IPs, tags, route tables, ENIs, VPC endpoints, EBS volumes, EBS snapshots, NAT gateways, network ACLs, flow logs, VPC peering, DHCP options, egress-only IGWs, managed prefix lists, VPN gateways/connections, launch templates, AMIs (register/deregister/describe), EC2 Fleet (CreateFleet, DescribeFleets). Instances exist in memory only — no real VMs launched. EC2 Fleet: instant-type synchronously launches instances and emits the Instances/Errors blocks; maintain/request return FleetId alone (FulfilledCapacity=0, ActivityStatus=pending_fulfillment) matching AWS async-fulfilment semantics; DefaultTargetCapacityType drives spot vs on-demand (not the FleetType enum); TotalTargetCapacity is round-robin distributed across every LaunchTemplateConfigs[*]×Overrides[*] slot; DescribeFleets on an unknown FleetId returns InvalidFleetId.NotFound. ENIs: AttachNetworkInterface records Attachment.AttachTime; DescribeNetworkInterfaces surfaces it as <attachTime> matching the AWS NetworkInterfaceAttachment shape (required by Cloud Custodian / Config rules that audit attachment age).
gotchas: By default RunInstances creates in-memory records only; since 1.5.0 RegisterImage can back an instance with a real container (opt-in), reachable and driven by ssm:SendCommand
DescribeImages returns a stub set of common AMI IDs
No actual networking — VPCs, subnets, security groups are metadata-only
EBS volumes are metadata-only — no real block storage

ecr.notes: Repository CRUD, image lifecycle, lifecycle policies, image tagging, batch operations. Stores manifest and layer metadata in-memory.
gotchas: Image layers are not stored — only manifests and metadata are tracked
No actual Docker registry protocol — images cannot be pushed/pulled via docker CLI
Lifecycle policy evaluation is not implemented

ecs.notes: 47 actions covering clusters, task definitions (multi-revision), services, tasks (RunTask with real Docker containers), capacity providers, tags, account settings, attributes, deployments, and agent state changes. RunTask starts real Docker containers via Docker socket when available; registers ECS Task Metadata V4 tokens. DeleteService marks the record INACTIVE instead of removing it (per the AWS contract: 'Services in the DRAINING or INACTIVE status can still be viewed with the DescribeServices API operation'); tasks are stopped synchronously, tags remain attached; re-creating with the same name is allowed once the prior incarnation is INACTIVE.
gotchas: Container execution requires Docker socket to be mounted
Without Docker, RunTask creates task records but no actual containers
Service desired count is stored but no auto-scaling or placement logic runs
ExecuteCommand returns a stub — no real interactive session

ecs_metadata.notes: ECS Task Metadata V4 endpoint (/v4/<token>, /v4/<token>/task, /v4/<token>/stats). Tokens registered by ecs.RunTask. State is volatile by design — stripped on persistence, cleared on reset.
gotchas: Stats endpoint returns empty/stub data — no real container metrics
Tokens are in-process only — not persisted across restarts

efs.notes: 17 operations: file systems (Create/Describe/Delete/Update), mount targets (Create/Describe/Delete/DescribeSecurityGroups/ModifySecurityGroups), access points (Create/Describe/Delete), tags (Tag/Untag/List plus legacy Create/Delete/Describe), lifecycle configuration, backup policy, account preferences. Control-plane CRUD only; no real filesystem.
gotchas: No real NFS filesystem — mount targets are metadata-only
Backup policy and lifecycle configuration are stored but not enforced

eks.notes: 28 operations: CreateCluster, DescribeCluster, ListClusters, DeleteCluster, CreateNodegroup, DescribeNodegroup, ListNodegroups, DeleteNodegroup, CreateAddon, DescribeAddon, ListAddons, UpdateAddon, DeleteAddon, AssociateEncryptionConfig, CreateAccessEntry, DescribeAccessEntry, ListAccessEntries, UpdateAccessEntry, DeleteAccessEntry, AssociateAccessPolicy, DisassociateAccessPolicy, ListAssociatedAccessPolicies, AssociateIdentityProviderConfig, DescribeIdentityProviderConfig, DisassociateIdentityProviderConfig, TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource. CreateCluster spawns a real k3s container (75 MB) with full K8s API server; kubectl, Helm, any K8s tooling work. Every k3s node now boots with the AWS-default topology.kubernetes.io/zone={region}a and topology.kubernetes.io/region={region} labels (matches the labels the AWS cloud-controller-manager emits on real EKS nodes), so Karpenter / Cluster Autoscaler / scheduler topologySpreadConstraints schedule pods without manual `kubectl label node`. Per-node-group label overrides belong on CreateNodegroup.labels — the AWS-shape-correct surface. Cascading delete removes nodegroups and k3s container. AssociateEncryptionConfig at /clusters/{name}/encryption-config/associate records KMS encryption config (rejects re-association). Access Entries (modern post-1.29 IAM bindings replacing the aws-auth ConfigMap) at /clusters/{name}/access-entries[/{principalArn}[/access-policies[/{policyArn}]]] support Crossplane accessentry.eks.aws.upbound.io and Terraform aws_eks_access_entry + aws_eks_access_policy_association; accessScope validated against {cluster, namespace}; deleting an access entry cascades its associated policies. OIDC discovery + JWKS served at the cluster's identity.oidc.issuer (now ministack-hosted at /oidc/id/{32-char-id}) so terraform's aws_iam_openid_connect_provider works against ministack. OIDC Identity Provider Config (Associate/Describe/Disassociate) at /clusters/{name}/identity-provider-configs/{verb}: one OIDC IdP per cluster regardless of name (any second associate returns ResourceInUseException); issuer+clientId+claims forwarded to k3s via --kube-apiserver-arg=oidc-*; identityProviderConfigArn stable across describes so Terraform/CDK/Pulumi don't see drift; tags reachable via ListTagsForResource(resourceArn=idp_arn); cluster status stays ACTIVE throughout (the work is in the returned update record). CFN AWS::EKS::Cluster and Nodegroup supported.
gotchas: Requires Docker socket for real k3s cluster creation
Cluster creation is async — status transitions from CREATING to ACTIVE in a background thread
Nodegroups are metadata-only — no actual worker nodes are provisioned
Addons are metadata-only — status flips to ACTIVE immediately, no real plugin installed in the k3s cluster
Access Entries are metadata-only — no real RBAC binding is created on the k3s cluster
k3s container uses the ministack Docker network for inter-service communication

AssociateIdentityProviderConfig / DisassociateIdentityProviderConfig restart the k3s container to apply --kube-apiserver-arg=oidc-* flags — this wipes in-cluster workloads (Pods/Deployments/Services); a warning is logged. Real AWS rolls config without affecting the data plane.

elasticache.notes: CreateCacheCluster spins up real Redis/Memcached Docker containers. Full replication group support with primary/replica topology. Subnet groups, parameter groups, user/user group CRUD, tags, describe events, failover.
gotchas: Requires Docker socket for real Redis/Memcached container creation
Container startup is non-blocking — status transitions from 'creating' to 'available' asynchronously
Without Docker, clusters are metadata-only stubs
PERSIST_STATE=1 respawns containers on boot

emr.notes: 17+ operations: RunJobFlow, DescribeCluster, ListClusters, TerminateJobFlows, ModifyCluster, SetTerminationProtection, SetVisibleToAllUsers, AddJobFlowSteps, DescribeStep, ListSteps, CancelSteps, AddInstanceFleet, ListInstanceFleets, ModifyInstanceFleet, AddInstanceGroups, ListInstanceGroups, ModifyInstanceGroups, ListBootstrapActions, AddTags, RemoveTags, GetBlockPublicAccessConfiguration, PutBlockPublicAccessConfiguration. Control-plane stub; clusters do not run actual Spark/Hadoop.
gotchas: No actual EMR cluster execution — clusters are metadata records only
Steps immediately complete — no real job processing
Instance fleets and groups are stored but no EC2 instances are launched

eventbridge.notes: 40+ operations: event buses (Create/Update/Delete/List/Describe), rules (Put/Delete/List/Describe/Enable/Disable), targets (Put/Remove/ListTargetsByRule/ListRuleNamesByTarget), PutEvents, TestEventPattern, tags, archives (Create/Delete/Describe/Update/List), permissions (Put/Remove), connections (Create/Describe/Delete/List/Update/Deauthorize), API destinations (Create/Describe/Delete/List/Update), replays (Start/Describe/List/Cancel), endpoints, partner/SaaS event sources. Lambda target dispatch on PutEvents; S3 EventBridge notifications; archives capture matching events and StartReplay re-dispatches them in a background thread.
gotchas: SaaS/partner event source APIs are control-plane stubs — no real third-party integration
Connection authorization is stored but not used for actual API destination calls
Replay re-dispatches events in a background thread — timing is not guaranteed
TestEventPattern uses fnmatch-based matching, not the full AWS event pattern grammar

firehose.notes: 11 operations: CreateDeliveryStream, DeleteDeliveryStream, DescribeDeliveryStream, ListDeliveryStreams, PutRecord, PutRecordBatch, UpdateDestination, TagDeliveryStream, UntagDeliveryStream, ListTagsForDeliveryStream, StartDeliveryStreamEncryption, StopDeliveryStreamEncryption. Destinations: ExtendedS3, S3 (deprecated alias), HttpEndpoint. S3 destination records are written synchronously to the local S3 emulator. DeliveryStreamType=KinesisStreamAsSource is fully wired: records put into the source Kinesis stream are forwarded to the configured ExtendedS3 / S3 destination inline on PutRecord / PutRecords (same fan-out pattern as SNS→SQS), honoring Prefix and DeliveryStartTimestamp. ProcessingConfiguration.Processors[].Type=Lambda is invoked per batch with the AWS-shape event ({invocationId, deliveryStreamArn, region, records:[{recordId, approximateArrivalTimestamp, data(base64)}]}); response {records:[{recordId, result, data}]} with result Ok|Dropped|ProcessingFailed; Lambda failures pass records through unchanged (best-effort per AWS).
gotchas: HttpEndpoint destination buffers records in-memory — no actual HTTP delivery
S3 destination requires the target bucket to already exist in the S3 emulator
No buffering interval or size-based batching — S3 writes happen synchronously on each PutRecord

glue.notes: Full Data Catalog: databases, tables, partitions, connections, crawlers, jobs, job runs, security configurations, classifiers, partition indexes, crawler metrics, tags, triggers, workflows, user-defined functions. Partition actions complete: BatchCreatePartition / BatchGetPartition / BatchUpdatePartition / CreatePartition / DeletePartition / GetPartition / GetPartitions. BatchUpdatePartition matches the per-entry AWS shape — Entries[*].{PartitionValueList, PartitionInput} in, Errors[*].{PartitionValueList, ErrorDetail{ErrorCode, ErrorMessage}} out — and preserves CreationTime / refreshes LastAccessTime. CreateDatabase honors the top-level Tags field (stored against the database ARN; cleaned up on DeleteDatabase). UpdateTable supports VersionId-based optimistic concurrency: table records carry a monotonically-increasing VersionId (string, per the AWS Table output shape); a stale VersionId returns ConcurrentModificationException; calls that omit VersionId keep last-write-wins for back-compat. UserDefinedFunction APIs (Create/Update/Delete/Get/GetMany) at AWSGlue.<verb> — records carry FunctionName, DatabaseName, ClassName, OwnerName, OwnerType, CreateTime, ResourceUris, CatalogId; GetUserDefinedFunctions honors the AWS-required Pattern glob. Python shell jobs execute via subprocess. Spark jobs (glueetl/gluestreaming) run on the official amazon/aws-glue-libs PySpark image (GlueVersion 4.0 / 3.0) on MiniStack's Docker network. Override image via GLUE_DOCKER_IMAGE. Crawlers transition through RUNNING state with configurable timer (GLUE_CRAWLER_RUN_SECONDS). Background paths (StartJobRun worker thread + crawler finish Timer) carry the request's contextvars via contextvars.copy_context().run(...), so on-disk script resolution and crawler completion both work under non-default accounts (mirrors the established stepfunctions.py / rds.py idiom).
gotchas: Spark jobs require Docker socket and pull the ~2GB amazon/aws-glue-libs image on first use
Python shell jobs run as local subprocesses — no isolation from the MiniStack process
Crawlers run a timer but do not actually crawl S3 data to infer schemas
Without Docker, Spark job runs will fail

iam.notes: 70+ actions: users, groups, roles, policies (managed + inline), access keys (Create/List/Delete/Update/GetLastUsed), instance profiles, service-linked roles, OIDC providers (Create/Get/List/Delete), SAML providers (Create/Get/List/Update/Delete), login profiles (Create/Get/Update/Delete), virtual MFA devices (Create/Enable/Deactivate/Delete/List/Resync), GetAccountAuthorizationDetails, Access Advisor (GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails/GetServiceLastAccessedDetails), attached/inline policies for users and roles, assume role policy updates, SimulatePrincipalPolicy, SimulateCustomPolicy, TagRole/UntagRole/ListRoleTags, TagUser/UntagUser/ListUserTags, TagPolicy/UntagPolicy/ListPolicyTags. AWS-managed policy seeds carry the verbatim AWS documents (not the wildcard Allow * fallback) for AdministratorAccess, PowerUserAccess, ReadOnlyAccess, SecurityAudit, IAMFullAccess, IAMReadOnlyAccess, AmazonS3FullAccess, AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess, AmazonEC2FullAccess, AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess, AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess, AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole, AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole, AmazonSQSFullAccess, AmazonSNSFullAccess, AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy, CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy, CloudWatchLogsFullAccess, AWSCloudFormationFullAccess, AmazonEKSClusterPolicy, AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEKSServicePolicy — so GetPolicyVersion returns the real action lists and Terraform diffs / policy simulators behave the same as real AWS.
gotchas: Policies are not evaluated by default; set AUTH=true to evaluate the caller's policies and return 403 AccessDenied on a disallowed action (SigV4 signatures are never validated either way)
SimulatePrincipalPolicy/SimulateCustomPolicy return stub results
Access key rotation is tracked but credentials are not validated on requests

imds.notes: IMDSv1 + IMDSv2; default credential chain falls through to a ministack-instance-role document with ASIA* session creds. Point SDKs via AWS_EC2_METADATA_SERVICE_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4566. Set MINISTACK_IMDS_V2_REQUIRED=1 to require the token PUT.
gotchas: No AccountScopedDict — returns global credentials
Not persisted — tokens are in-process only
Credentials are synthetic — not tied to any real IAM role

inspector2.notes: 14 operations covering Enable/Disable/ListFindings/BatchGetFindingDetails/ListCoverage/ListCoverageStatistics/ListFindingAggregations/SearchVulnerabilities plus filter and tag CRUD. Deterministic stub vulnerability findings for ECR images, Lambda functions, and EC2 instances.
gotchas: Findings are deterministic stubs — no actual vulnerability scanning is performed
SearchVulnerabilities returns pre-defined stub results

iot.notes: AWS IoT Core: Things, ThingTypes, ThingGroups, certificates via local CA, IoT Policies with versioning, DescribeEndpoint. Supported KeySpec values include RSA (2048/4096), ECC (SECG_P256K1, NIST P-256/384/521), Edwards25519 (ECC_NIST_EDWARDS25519 — pure Ed25519 via ED25519_SHA_512 with MessageType=RAW; ED25519_PH_SHA_512 advertised in SigningAlgorithms but Sign/Verify returns UnsupportedOperationException until Ed25519ph lands, since the cryptography library doesn't expose the dom2 prefix and producing pure-Ed25519 signatures under that name would be wire-incompatible with real AWS KMS), and symmetric keys.

lambda_svc.notes: 40+ operations: CreateFunction (now accepts DurableConfig), DeleteFunction, GetFunction, GetFunctionConfiguration, ListFunctions (paginated), Invoke (RequestResponse/Event/DryRun), UpdateFunctionCode, UpdateFunctionConfiguration, PublishVersion, ListVersionsByFunction, CreateAlias, GetAlias, UpdateAlias, DeleteAlias, ListAliases, AddPermission, RemovePermission, GetPolicy, ListTags, TagResource, UntagResource, PublishLayerVersion, GetLayerVersion, GetLayerVersionByArn, ListLayerVersions, DeleteLayerVersion, ListLayers, AddLayerVersionPermission, RemoveLayerVersionPermission, GetLayerVersionPolicy, CreateEventSourceMapping, DeleteEventSourceMapping, GetEventSourceMapping, ListEventSourceMappings, UpdateEventSourceMapping, PutFunctionConcurrency, GetFunctionConcurrency, DeleteFunctionConcurrency, CreateFunctionUrlConfig, GetFunctionUrlConfig, UpdateFunctionUrlConfig, DeleteFunctionUrlConfig, ListFunctionUrlConfigs. **Durable Functions (Durable Execution)** — CheckpointDurableExecution, GetDurableExecutionState, GetDurableExecution, GetDurableExecutionHistory, ListDurableExecutionsByFunction, StopDurableExecution, plus the three external callback ops (SendDurableExecutionCallbackSuccess, SendDurableExecutionCallbackFailure, SendDurableExecutionCallbackHeartbeat). Resume scheduler fires WAIT expiries, callback timeouts, and step-retry backoffs. State persists across restarts. Python and Node.js runtimes execute with warm worker pool; provided.al2023/provided.al2 runtimes execute via Docker RIE. Code via ZipFile, S3Bucket/S3Key, or ImageUri. SQS, Kinesis, and DynamoDB Streams event source mappings. Invoke LogResult returns user output + traceback on error. TracingConfig.Mode=Active injects _X_AMZN_TRACE_ID (Root=1-<8hex>-<24hex>;Parent=<16hex>;Sampled=1) into the runtime per invocation so the AWS X-Ray SDK works on the warm worker, provided runtime, and local subprocess executors. Layers attached via CreateFunction or UpdateFunctionConfiguration surface the layer version's real CodeSize on GetFunctionConfiguration.Layers[*].CodeSize (was hardcoded 0); UpdateFunctionConfiguration recycles the $LATEST warm worker when worker-affecting fields change (Layers, Runtime, Handler, Environment, MemorySize, Architectures, VpcConfig, FileSystemConfigs), so a layer attached after the first invoke is actually mounted at /opt/layer_N for the next call and the handler can import from it. Docker executor (DinD): layer cp extracts into /opt with arcname=layer_N instead of put_archive at /opt/layer_N (which 404s because the destination subdir doesn't pre-exist in the RIE image); the docker warm-container pool is also reaped on UpdateFunctionConfiguration / DeleteFunction so reused pre-attach containers don't serve invokes after a layer is attached.
gotchas: Python/Node.js run in-process by default — no container isolation unless using provided.* runtimes
provided.* runtimes (Go, Rust, C++) require Docker socket for RIE execution
Event source mappings poll in background threads — timing is best-effort
ImageUri-based functions require Docker to pull and run the image
Warm worker pool reuses processes — global state can leak between invocations
TracingConfig.Mode=Active is not supported on the docker RIE executor (AWS RIE drops X-Ray upstream) — logs a warning

lambda_durable.notes: AWS Lambda Durable Functions (Durable Execution) preview API (2025-12-01). 9 operations: CheckpointDurableExecution, GetDurableExecutionState, GetDurableExecution, GetDurableExecutionHistory, ListDurableExecutionsByFunction, StopDurableExecution, plus the three external callback ops SendDurableExecutionCallbackSuccess, SendDurableExecutionCallbackFailure, SendDurableExecutionCallbackHeartbeat. CreateFunction accepts DurableConfig. A resume scheduler fires WAIT expiries, callback timeouts (Callback.Timeout / Callback.Heartbeat), and step-retry backoffs (NextAttemptDelaySeconds). State persists across MiniStack restarts — the in-memory callback index is rebuilt from restored executions on boot and pending timers are re-armed. End-to-end verified against the official aws-durable-execution-sdk-python 1.5.0 and aws-durable-execution-sdk-java 2.44.13.
gotchas: Preview API — AWS may revise the wire shapes before GA

rds.notes: CreateDBInstance spins up real Postgres/MySQL Docker container; returns actual host:port endpoint. Non-blocking create; daemon thread waits for container liveness, sets DBInstanceStatus to 'available' or 'failed'. PERSIST_STATE=1 respawns containers on boot. When ministack itself runs in Docker, the auto-detected ministack Docker network is used and DescribeDBInstances reports container_ip:container_port (reachable from apps on the same network). For remote-ministack-in-Docker deployments where external clients can't reach that network, set MINISTACK_RDS_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT=1 (and MINISTACK_HOST=<remote-ip>) — DescribeDBInstances then returns {MINISTACK_HOST, host_port}, the externally-reachable host-published Docker port. Off by default, so existing deployments are unchanged. AWS-shape compatible: Endpoint.Port is an arbitrary integer (1150-65535) per botocore.

s3.notes: Full S3 implementation: CreateBucket, DeleteBucket, ListBuckets, HeadBucket, PutObject, GetObject, DeleteObject, HeadObject, CopyObject, ListObjectsV1/V2, DeleteObjects (batch), multipart upload (Create/UploadPart/Complete/Abort/List/ListParts), object tagging, ListObjectVersions, bucket sub-resources (Policy/Versioning/Encryption/Lifecycle/CORS/ACL/Tagging/Notification/Logging/Accelerate/RequestPayment/Website), Object Lock (retention/legal hold enforcement on delete), replication (Put/Get/Delete), range requests (206), Content-MD5 validation, encoding-type=url. PutObject checksums end-to-end: SHA256 / SHA1 / CRC32 client-supplied values are accepted, x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm triggers server-side compute, mismatch rejected with BadDigest. Get / HeadObject surface checksum headers under x-amz-checksum-mode: ENABLED (never on 206 Partial Content — a whole-object checksum can't validate sliced bytes). CopyObject propagates the source checksum (or computes/validates against a different algorithm requested via x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm). Versioned reads honor per-version checksums. Checksums persist across restart via the on-disk meta sidecar. CRC32C / CRC64NVME are rejected with InvalidRequest rather than silently round-tripping unverifiable client-supplied values (the dep ministack would need to compute them isn't bundled per the no-new-deps rule). CreateBucket / DeleteBucket account-scope the on-disk bucket directory to match the canonical object writer (_object_disk_path), so the persisted layout is end-to-end account-scoped under DATA_DIR/<account>/<bucket>/<key>.
gotchas: Optional disk persistence via S3_PERSIST=1 or S3_DATA_DIR
ACLs are stored but not enforced on access
Bucket policies are stored but not evaluated
Lifecycle rules are stored but not automatically executed
Replication configuration is stored but objects are not actually replicated

Glacier / Deep Archive restore is emulated: an object in GLACIER/DEEP_ARCHIVE is unreadable (InvalidObjectState) until RestoreObject completes, in seconds rather than AWS's hours; GLACIER_IR stays readable
